rfi.title: Sudan rights groups blame RSF paramilitary for drone strikes that hit civilians
rfi.description: Drone strikes blamed on the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) have killed at least 23 civilians and wounded 19 others in the Sudanese city of El-Obeid, local monitoring groups have said, as the use of armed drones continues to spread across the country in its more than three-year war.

rfi.title: What's in the landmark EU migration reform hardening border protections?
rfi.description: A major reform of European migration rules aimed at hardening border procedures and overhauling the asylum process comes into force on Friday.

rfi.title: Two French cities impose curfews for under-16s during World Cup
rfi.description: The mayors of Toulouse and Clermont-Ferrand are imposing nighttime curfews on children under 16 during the 2026 World Cup. They say the move is aimed at preventing the violent unrest seen after Paris Saint-Germain's Champions League victory last month.

rfi.title: British art 'giant' David Hockney dies aged 88
rfi.description: British artist David Hockney, one of the most influential and defining figures in contemporary art, whose paintings captured the world in brilliant colour, has died aged 88, his publicist announced Friday.

rfi.title: Rise in adulterated cannabis in France, as edible CBD ban shakes industry
rfi.description: Cannabis use in France is once again under scrutiny, with a drugs monitor reporting a sharp rise in adulterated products on the illegal market, and risky new products entering the legal CBD market. To address the issue of mislabelled products, France has banned edible CBD products, raising concerns in the cannabis industry.

rfi.title: Israeli and Palestinian groups urge action on two-state solution in Paris
rfi.description: Israeli and Palestinian civil society groups will meet in Paris on Friday to urge the international community not to abandon a two-state solution, as France seeks to keep the issue on the agenda amid the ongoing war in the Middle East.

rfi.title: Ebola outbreak spreads in DRC as misinformation hampers response
rfi.description: Authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo have launched an online campaign to tackle growing mistrust surrounding a deadly Ebola outbreak. The World Health Organization (WHO) says misinformation is hampering efforts to contain the haemorrhagic fever, which broke out in the eastern province of Ituri on 15 May.

rfi.title: Mexico brush past ill-disciplined South Africa to launch World Cup party
rfi.description: Mexico's Julian Quinones and Raul Jimenez punished an indisciplined South Africa on Thursday night in the opening match of the 2026 World Cup.

rfi.title: Man linked to Dominique Pelicot on trial accused of drugging and raping partner
rfi.description: A man with ties to convicted French mass rapist Dominique Pelicot is on trial in Lyon, accused of drugging and raping his partner while filming the assaults and streaming them online.

rfi.title: Children in danger 'not heard' in France, rights lawyer warns after Lyhanna death
rfi.description: The abduction and killing of 11-year-old French schoolgirl Lyhanna has catapaulted child protection to the top of France's political agenda – with President Emmanuel Macron on Wednesday calling for full accountability and the government pledging full transparency. As investigators examine possible failures by the justice system, child rights lawyer Dominique Attias tells RFI professionals have been warning for years that vulnerable children are not being protected.

rfi.title: Killing of gay man to be investigated as homophobic crime following protests
rfi.description: Police investigating the murder of a young gay man in the eastern French city of Metz have said the case will now be treated as a homophobic crime, after protestations from rights groups and politicians.

rfi.title: RFI denounces violation of press freedom after French reporter barred by Israel
rfi.description: RFI has condemned Israel's decision to refuse entry to journalist Alice Froussard, describing the move as "an obstacle to press freedom". Froussard, who reports on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict for French media, including RFI, was turned away on arrival at Tel Aviv airport and sent back without explanation.

rfi.title: Climate report shows 1.5C limit on global warming will be breached by 2030
rfi.description: Human-induced global warming is on track to reach 1.5C around 2030, a group of leading scientists said on Thursday.

rfi.title: Fifa grants World Cup accreditation to jailed French journalist Christophe Gleizes
rfi.description: In a move hailed by press freedom campaigners as an important gesture of solidarity, Fifa has issued World Cup accreditation to French sports journalist Christophe Gleizes, who has been detained in Algeria for more than a year.

rfi.title: French pop star Patrick Bruel charged with rape and sexual assault
rfi.description: French singer and actor Patrick Bruel has been charged with rape, attempted rape, sexual assault and sexual harassment, prosecutors said on Wednesday, in a case that now involves accusations by more than 20 women.

rfi.title: Amnesty accuses Israel of ‘ethnic cleansing’ of West Bank Bedouin communities
rfi.description: Amnesty International has accused Israel of carrying out what it described as a state-led campaign of “ethnic cleansing” against Bedouin and herding communities in the occupied West Bank, saying the measures were intended to accelerate the annexation of Palestinian territory.

rfi.title: Europe faces growing threat from synthetic opioids and new drugs, report warns
rfi.description: Highly potent synthetic opioids are spreading through Europe's fast-changing drug market, linked to hundreds of deaths as traffickers shift to smaller ports and new smuggling methods, the European Union Drugs Agency (EUDA) has warned.

rfi.title: European heatwave drives world's second-hottest May on record
rfi.description: The world experienced its second-hottest May on record in 2026 as an unusually early and intense heatwave swept across Europe, setting new temperature records across the continent, the European Union's Copernicus Climate Change Service said on Wednesday.

euronews.title: EU energy ministers eye jet fuel reserves as Strait of Hormuz crisis threatens supply
euronews.description: With the peak summer season drawing near, EU energy ministers are wary that jet fuel supply may be further strained, even as analysts see "sharp movement" towards greater jet fuel production within European refineries.

euronews.title: Washington plans to slash fighter jets and warships to NATO in Europe, US media report
euronews.description: The reported cutbacks come as European nations race to bolster their defence capacities since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 sparked fears that Moscow could attack a NATO country.

euronews.title: Pope urges 'reciprocal' integration between migrants and host countries
euronews.description: During his visit to Tenerife, the pontiff called for integration based on rights and duties, urging migrants to learn the language, obey the law and join in community life.

euronews.title: What to know about the EU's new migration and asylum reforms as they come into effect
euronews.description: The bloc’s new migration rules take effect on Friday after months of political wrangling. Here are the changes that are now in force.

euronews.title: ‘Land of the fulfilled  farmers’: Why the grass seems to grow greener in Austria
euronews.description: Austria has repeatedly been acknowledged as a success story in the intergenerational renewal of its farming sector. A combination of hard work at family-run farms, strong public support, qualitative professional training and engaged consumers is revitalizing entire rural communities.

euronews.title: Disaster drills helped prevent more deaths when quake hit Philippines, officials say
euronews.description: The numbers of dead and missing were considerably lowered after multiple verifications, the Office of Civil Defence said in a statement.

euronews.title: Gaza Families search ruins after Israeli strikes hit homes
euronews.description: Palestinians in central Gaza searched through rubble on 12 June after Israeli strikes destroyed homes in Deir al-Balah and the Maghazi refugee camp, leaving dozens of displaced families without shelter and struggling to recover their belongings.

euronews.title: How EU countries watered down 'solidarity' plans to relocate asylum seekers
euronews.description: A new migration law introducing "mandatory solidarity" has been all but circumvented by the EU's member states, who will relocate fewer than 9,000 asylum seekers this year – even after the annual minimum was set at 30,000.

euronews.title: Everything you need to know about the Jared Kushner resort protests in Albania
euronews.description: The European Commission has warned Albania that it must act now to avoid jeopardising its bid to join the bloc, which requires it to comply with EU environmental rules.

euronews.title: 'Do not ever use my music': Ariana Grande slams the White House over ICE video
euronews.description: The White House has repeatedly faced criticism for using popular music in social media posts without the approval of the artists involved. This time, the Trump administration has decided to hop on a trending track by Ariana Grande.

euronews.title: San Andreas Fault reaches highest stress level in 1,000 years
euronews.description: Researchers report that tectonic stress on the major San Andreas and San Jacinto fault systems has climbed to its highest levels in a millennium, and in some sections has already surpassed them.

euronews.title: Georgieva: Europeans must invest 'together'
euronews.description: European economic conditions "have worsened," International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said, as the IMF is now "downgrading" its growth projections and "uplifting" its inflation forecasts. Georgieva recommends that the EU invest "together" and "wisely".

euronews.title: Elon Musk's SpaceX IPO: the capitalist space revolution begins
euronews.description: World’s biggest IPO: Elon Musk wants to raise $75bn for SpaceX, making him Earth’s first trillionaire, as Rainer Zitelmann explains in an opinion piece for Euronews how it came about and what happens next.

euronews.title: Podcast: The most political World Cup to date?
euronews.description: What makes the 2026 World Cup so political? What does the entry of the EU Migration and Asylum Pact mean in reality? The two questions we answer on Brussels, My Love? the podcast.

euronews.title: Ukraine's drone strikes are methodically cutting Crimea off from Russia
euronews.description: Ukraine has significantly intensified its strikes on military and energy sites in and around Russia-occupied Crimea in what is seen as Kyiv’s deliberate strategy of cutting the annexed Ukrainian peninsula off from Russia.

euronews.title: Brussels joins growing list of European cities banning shared e-scooters over safety concerns
euronews.description: The Belgian capital will remove rental e-scooters from its streets from January 2027, citing rising accident rates, pavement clutter and their increasing use by organised crime groups. Shared bikes and e-bikes will remain available instead.

euronews.title: Viral Dua Lipa wedding photos were AI-generated
euronews.description: A series of fake images purporting to show pop star Dua Lipa celebrating her wedding in the Sicilian town of Palermo have fooled users and even some digital media outlets.

euronews.title: What if Trump actually seized Kharg Island?
euronews.description: Kharg Island is a small coral outcrop off the coast of Iran that handles around 90% of the country's crude oil exports, making it key to Tehran's economy.

lemonde.title: En Turquie, comment le régime d’Erdogan a bâti un capitalisme de connivence
lemonde.description: En moins d’un quart de siècle, la formation islamo-conservatrice du président turc, Recep Tayyip Erdogan, a donné les clés de l’économie du pays à un cercle restreint issu d’une classe d’affaires loyale et de relations clientélistes.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre au Moyen-Orient : le choc énergétique sera « persistant » quelle que soit « l’évolution géopolitique à court terme », estime le gouverneur de la Banque de France
lemonde.description: L’institution monétaire, dont Emmanuel Moulin vient de prendre la tête, doit annoncer mardi ses prévisions actualisées pour la croissance française, attendues en baisse par rapport à la prévision initiale de 0,9 % en 2026.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Raphaël Glucksmann veut tenter d’écarter les doutes lors d’un meeting à haut risque à Aubervilliers
lemonde.description: Le fondateur de Place publique, qui organise un rassemblement samedi 13 juin, s’est donné trois mois avant d’annoncer son éventuelle candidature à l’Elysée. Cette temporisation et la dynamique de Jean-Luc Mélenchon suscitent des interrogations à gauche.

lemonde.title: L’encadrement des loyers salué par les locataires d’Ile-de-France malgré les menaces qui pèsent sur le dispositif
lemonde.description: Le gouvernement envisage de mettre un terme à ce dispositif expérimental, qui a pourtant permis à des locataires de communes où il est en place, telles Paris ou Aubervilliers (Seine-Saint-Denis), d’obtenir une baisse salutaire des loyers, que la pénurie de logements fait grimper en flèche.

lemonde.title: David Hockney, grand peintre britannique, est mort à l’âge de 88 ans
lemonde.description: Mondialement connu, notamment pour sa toile « A Bigger Splash » et ses « Pool Paintings », l’artiste britannique a produit une œuvre entre le pop art et l’hyperréalisme, n’hésitant pas à utiliser les nouvelles technologies (photocopieur, iPhone, iPad…) comme source d’inspiration. Il s’est éteint jeudi 11 juin à 88 ans.

lemonde.title: Coupe du monde 2026 : l’ouverture du tournoi, à Mexico, laisse un sentiment contrasté, selon la presse étrangère
lemonde.description: Le Mondial de football a débuté, jeudi soir, à Mexico. La cérémonie d’ouverture a été très courte. Des affrontements se sont produits aux abords du stade Azteca entre des manifestants et la police. Et la victoire du Mexique contre l’Afrique du Sud (2-0) a donné lieu à un festival de… cartons rouges.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : un tir du missile balistique russe Orechnik redouté par l’armée de l’air ukrainienne dans les prochaines vingt-quatre heures
lemonde.description: La Russie a frappé à trois reprises avec l’Orechnik, à la fin 2024, début 2026 et le 24 mai. A chaque fois, le missile ne portait pas de charge nucléaire. Un quatrième Orechnik s’est écrasé sur une agglomération de l’autoproclamée « république populaire de Donetsk », le 23 mai.

lemonde.title: Mort de Lyhanna : revivez la journée d’hommage à la collégienne de Fleurance, et retrouvez les réactions politiques

lemonde.description: Installé à Berlin depuis sa libération, cet ancien député municipal de Moscou lance, vendredi, un nouveau parti anti-Kremlin : Russie pacifique. Une initiative accueillie avec scepticisme par certaines figures de la dissidence à l’étranger.

lemonde.title: « Au Royaume-Uni, faute de stratégie électorale, le Parti travailliste pourrait s’enfoncer dans un déclin durable »

lemonde.description: L’avocat général s’est opposé, jeudi 11 juin, à la révision réclamée depuis près d’un demi-siècle par les ayants droit de ces deux hommes condamnés pour meurtre, et morts en 2003 et 2009. Décision le 2 juillet.

lemonde.title: Mort de Nahel : la Cour de cassation annule la requalification des faits en « violences » et rouvre la voie à un possible procès pour meurtre
lemonde.description: La chambre de l’instruction de la cour d’appel de Versailles « n’a pas justifié sa décision » de requalification, a estimé la plus haute instance judiciaire française. L’affaire est donc renvoyée devant la cour d’appel de Versailles, qui devra statuer de nouveau sur le chef pour lequel est renvoyé le policier Florian M.

lemonde.title: Frank Michael, le chanteur de « Toutes les femmes sont belles », est mort à 79 ans
lemonde.description: Le chanteur belge d’origine italienne, connu pour ses chansons à l’eau de rose, revendiquait des dizaines de Disques d’or et « entre 15 millions et 20 millions » de disques vendus, en France, en Belgique, en Suisse, au Canada, en Italie ou en Allemagne.

lemonde.description: Les stupéfiants ont envahi la vie des Français. Dans le milieu professionnel, leur consommation s’est également banalisée, pour tenir le rythme et rester performant. S’il vous est déjà arrivé d’en prendre au travail, faites-nous part de votre expérience.

france24fr.title: Abdelaziz Rahabi : "La mémoire, pas un frein dans les relations entre Paris et Alger"
france24fr.description: Dans un entretien exclusif accordé à France 24, Abdelaziz Rahabi, ancien ministre algérien de la Communication, revient sur les relations qui se sont récemment tendues entre l'Algérie et la France. Pour lui, "la mémoire ne constitue pas du tout un frein aux relations". Il ajoute que l'Algérie n'a jamais demandé à la France de "se repentir sur son passé".

france24fr.title: Mort de David Hockney : hommage au peintre des piscines californiennes
france24fr.description: Le monde de l'art est en deuil après la disparition de David Hockney à l’âge de 88 ans. Figure majeure de l'art contemporain, le peintre britannique s'était imposé avec ses tableaux aux couleurs éclatantes, ses célèbres piscines californiennes et ses paysages baignés de lumière.

france24fr.title: Tunisie : les épreuves du baccalauréat agitées, entre coupures d'internet et soupçons de fraude
france24fr.description: En Tunisie, la session du baccalauréat a concerné 162 435 candidats cette année, dans un climat marqué par de fortes tensions autour de l’organisation des épreuves. Plusieurs incidents ont été signalés, entre soupçons de fraude, fuites de sujets et perturbations du réseau internet durant les examens. Une enseignante a même été convoquée par la justice après avoir dénoncé la diffusion de sujets sur les réseaux sociaux.

france24fr.title: Côte d’Ivoire : les "déguerpissements" jettent des milliers de familles à la rue
france24fr.description: En Côte d’Ivoire, les opérations de "déguerpissement", qui visent la destruction de quartiers précaires jugés à risque par les autorités, ont repris en pleine saison des pluies. Depuis la semaine dernière, plusieurs dizaines de milliers d’habitants ont perdu leur logement, sans solution de relogement immédiate. Parmi eux, de nombreux élèves se retrouvent en grande difficulté, ayant perdu leurs documents administratifs et risquant de ne pas pouvoir passer leurs examens. Les précisions de Julia Gu

france24fr.title: RD Congo : la controverse du possible 3e mandat de Tshisekedi relancée
france24fr.description: En République démocratique du Congo, l’Assemblée nationale a adopté une proposition de loi sur l’organisation d’un référendum, ravivant les débats sur une réforme constitutionnelle. L’opposition y voit une manœuvre ouvrant la voie à un troisième mandat pour Félix Tshisekedi, tandis que la majorité continue de défendre un changement de la Constitution. Les précisions de la correspondante de France 24 en RDC, Aurélie Bazzara Kibangula.

france24fr.title: Afrique du Sud : des milliers d’étrangers déplacés après des violences xénophobes à Durban
france24fr.description: À Durban, en Afrique du Sud, des milliers d’étrangers ont été contraints de quitter leur domicile après des manifestations anti-immigrés le mois dernier. Beaucoup, principalement originaires de RDC ou du Nigeria, vivent depuis dans des campements de fortune sans accès à l’eau ni aux toilettes, tandis que les tensions et agressions se multiplient dans la ville. Face à une situation jugée de plus en plus critique, les déplacés appellent à l’aide des autorités et de l’ONU.

france24fr.title: À New York, la Coupe du monde s’invite dans la rue pour les enfants des quartiers populaires
france24fr.description: À New York, l’administration du maire Zohran Mamdani développe des programmes de football de rue pour permettre aux enfants des quartiers populaires de vivre la Coupe du monde, malgré le prix élevé des billets. Entre enthousiasme local, critique de l’inaccessibilité des stades et débats sur la responsabilité de la FIFA, le tournoi de football se joue aussi en dehors des tribunes, dans les rues du Queens.

france24fr.title: Albanie : la contestation monte contre le projet immobilier Kushner-Trump
france24fr.description: En Albanie, un vaste projet immobilier porté par Jared Kushner et Ivanka Trump visant à transformer l’île de Sazan en complexe hôtelier de luxe suscite une forte contestation. Entre manifestations à Tirana, soutien controversé du gouvernement et mises en garde de Bruxelles sur l’impact environnemental, le projet cristallise les tensions politiques dans le pays, et pourrait compromettre la candidature de l'Albanie à l'UE

france24fr.title: Migration : l'objectif du pacte européen, "décourager les entrées irrégulières sur le sol européen"
france24fr.description: Une grande réforme de la politique migratoire européenne entre en vigueur vendredi. Deux ans après avoir été adoptée, elle entend modifier en profondeur la gestion des demandes d’asile dans l’UE. La journaliste Charlotte Boitiaux d'InfoMigrants explique l'application concrète de ce nouveau pacte européen en France, notamment dans les aéroports, qui sont les seules frontières extérieures de l'UE pour le pays. Selon elle, "tout l'intérêt du pacte asile, c'est de décourager les entrées irrégulières

france24fr.title: Mondial-2026 : les Léopards de la RD Congo arrivent aux États-Unis
france24fr.description: Les joueurs de la République démocratique du Congo, dont la préparation a été perturbée par des inquiétudes liées au virus Ebola, ont été autorisés à entrer aux États-Unis par les autorités pour disputer le Mondial-2026. Des supporters accueillent la délégation des Léopards en musique à leur arrivée à leur hôtel à Houston.

france24fr.title: Le Brexit : dix ans de chaos et de regrets ?
france24fr.description: Le 23 juin 2016, le Royaume-Uni a choisi de quitter l'Union européenne avec 52% de voix pour et 48% contre. Le résultat du référendum a provoqué un séisme politique que peu d'experts avaient vu venir. Dix ans après, Billet Retour se penche sur l'impact de cette décision historique. Comment le Brexit a t-il changé le pays ? Le niveau de vie des Britanniques s'est-il amélioré depuis ? Quelles ont été les conséquences pour l'économie et des secteurs clés comme l'agriculture ?

france24fr.title: Chine-États-Unis : Macron médiateur ?
france24fr.description: Alors que le sommet du G7 2026 organisé par Emmanuel Macron à Evian du 15 au 17 juin approche, le président français exhorte la Chine, les Etats-Unis et l'Europe à "agir avec urgence en vue d'une coordination de leur politique économique pour résorber les déséquilibres mondiaux". Les explications avec David Baverez, investisseur et essayiste, auteur de "Bienvenue en économie de guerre", éditions Novice, 2024.

france24fr.title: Aux Canaries, le pape Léon XIV réitère son soutien aux migrants tout en les incitant à l'intégration
france24fr.description: Au terme de son voyage d'une semaine en Espagne, le pape Léon XIV a répété son soutien aux migrants, vendredi aux Canaries, alors que la route migratoire vers l'Espagne via l'archipel est l'une des plus meurtrières d'Europe. Le pape a encouragé les migrants à s'intégrer, tout en rappelant aux citoyens espagnols leurs "devoirs" en matière d'accueil.

france24fr.title: Gianni Infantino et Donald Trump : une bromance politique qui va trop loin ?
france24fr.description: Le président de la FIFA, Gianni Infantino, a multiplié les gestes de proximité envers le président Donald Trump, de sa présence à son investiture en 2025 à la remise d'une distinction présentée comme un « prix de la paix » de la FIFA. Une relation jugée trop étroite par certains observateurs, qui estiment qu'elle entre en contradiction avec le principe de neutralité politique que la FIFA est censée respecter.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : à Houston, au Texas, les prix sont prohibitifs pour les fans
france24fr.description: La plus grande Coupe du monde de l’histoire débute cette année aux États-Unis, au Canada et au Mexique. Avec 48 équipes et 104 matchs, le tournoi promet d’attirer des millions de supporters à travers l’Amérique du Nord. À Houston, où sept rencontres sont programmées, les organisateurs affichent leur optimisme. Mais certains hôtels peinent à remplir leurs chambres et de nombreux supporters dénoncent des billets devenus inaccessibles. Reportage de Pierrick Leurent.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle 2027 : déjà des soupçons d’ingérence étrangère à dix mois du scrutin
france24fr.description: À dix mois de la présidentielle de 2027, le gouvernement français alerte sur de possibles tentatives d’ingérence étrangère dans le scrutin. Le Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu évoque des  "menaces lourdes", après plusieurs signalements et enquêtes ouvertes sur des opérations d’influence numérique lors des récentes élections municipales.

france24fr.title: Le sumo fait son grand retour en France avec un tournoi historique à Paris
france24fr.description: Soixante-deux des meilleurs lutteurs de sumo au monde sont réunis ce week-end à Paris pour un tournoi exceptionnel, une première en France depuis 1995. Considérés comme de véritables célébrités au Japon, ces athlètes aux gabarits impressionnants profitent aussi de leur séjour pour découvrir la capitale française.

zeit.description: Offensichtlich wird nichts mehr fertig in Deutschland. Höchste Zeit, für eine Kurzanleitung, wie wir alle unsere Baustellen lieben lernen.

zeit.description: Müssen Amtsträger vor Beleidigungen besser geschützt werden? Die sächsische Justizministerin Constanze Geiert streitet mit Renate Künast von den Grünen.

zeit.description: Szechuan-Pfeffer und Chilipaste in einer Lasagne? Das passiert, wenn im Gewürzschrank Chaos herrscht. Doch manch kulinarisches Experiment wird eben unerwartet großartig!

observador.description: Portugal está de partida para Palm Beach, onde ficará concentrado durante o Mundial-2026, depois de vencer Chile e Nigéria nos últimos testes. Correu tudo bem? Não. Mas, como diz Ronaldo, "ganhou-se".

observador.title: Aliados do Futuro: vamos falar sobre inovação?
observador.description: A Aliados Consulting juntou-se ao Observador Lab para lançar um novo podcast, onde líderes e especialistas vão debater sustentabilidade, inovação e economia.

observador.title: Aeroporto novo: do plano à pista
observador.description: Neste episódio, explicamos como se planeia, desenha e constrói o novo aeroporto em Alcochete, uma infraestrutura que vai marcar a mobilidade, a economia e o território nas próximas décadas.

observador.title: "Bom filho a casa torna": André Silva reforça ataque
observador.description: Internacional português André Silva vai representar novamente o FC Porto, nove anos após ter saído do clube rumo ao AC Milan. Avançado de 30 anos chega aos azuis e brancos como reforço a custo zero.

observador.title: Parlamento aprova confisco de bens sem haver condenação
observador.description: Proposta de lei foi aprovada em Conselho de Ministros em 11 de dezembro de 2025. O decreto parlamentar segue agora para a Presidência da República para promulgação.

observador.title: Parlamento aprova medidas para acelerar processos na Justiça
observador.description: Diploma foi aprovado com os votos a favor de PSD, Chega, IL, CDS-PP e PAN e votos contra de PS, Livre, PCP, BE e JPP. Decreto parlamentar segue agora para a Presidência da República para promulgação.

observador.title: Pode o México ser a grande surpresa deste Mundial?
observador.description: Após a vitória na estreia, o ambiente no estádio entusiasma a seleção mexicana, mas será que a equipa consegue manter a consistência na prova? O arranque da competição ficou marcado por três expulsões

observador.title: Infarmed manda retirar produto para alívio de queimaduras
observador.description: Autoridade nacional do medicamento concluiu que "o produto 'Calmidine' encontra-se no mercado indevidamente qualificado do ponto de vista regulamentar enquanto produto cosmético".

observador.title: Proibição de espetáculos pirotécnicos preocupa empresas
observador.description: "A proteção da floresta não pode servir de justificação para interpretações abusivas da lei nem para a penalização de uma atividade legal, licenciada e regulada", alerta associação.

observador.title: Parlamento aprova isenção de IRS a vítimas da Igreja
observador.description: Projetos de lei do BE, Chega, Livre e resolução do PAN foram aprovados na generalidade, seguindo para a especialidade onde será discutido mecanismo generalizado de isenção fiscal.

observador.title: Parlamento recomenda ao Governo que estude Dia da Defesa
observador.description: Iniciativa do Chega recomenda ao Governo que estude a alteração da Lei do Serviço Militar e respetivo regulamento, "no sentido de transformar o Dia da Defesa Nacional em Semana da Defesa Nacional".

observador.title: Entradas irregulares na UE caem 40% entre janeiro e maio
observador.description: Frontex registou 39 mil travessias irregulares das fronteiras externas da UE — uma redução que reflete a cooperação contínua com os países parceiros. Corredor da Líbia para Creta continua ativo.

observador.title: Florentino transfere-se a título definitivo para o Burnley
observador.description: Médio, de 26 anos, fez 33 encontros esta temporada ao serviço do Burnley, que terminou a Liga inglesa na 19.ª e penúltima posição e foi despromovido ao Championship.

observador.title: IA: 20% das empresas dizem ser fácil substituir licenciados
observador.description: Comércio e serviços estão entre as áreas com maior capacidade de substituição. Ainda assim, maioria das empresas continua a considerar difícil dispensar trabalhadores qualificados.

observador.title: Zapatero investigado por fraude fiscal e contrabando
observador.description: Joias com uma origem "não justificada neste momento" estão avaliadas em 1,3 milhões de euros. Zapatero afirma que são "heranças familiares e presentes", mas pode incorrer no crime de contrabando.

observador.title: TAP conclui reestruturação e limpa prejuízos
observador.description: Venda do handling e Cateringpor e devolução de 25 milhões de euros ao Estado eram os pontos que faltavam para cumprir plano. TAP reduz capital para absorver prejuízos passados antes da privatização.

nzz.title: SpaceX drängt an die Börse: Die Anleger warten gespannt auf den Handelsstart
nzz.description: Das Raumfahrtunternehmen hat erfolgreich 75 Milliarden Dollar an Aktienkapital aufgenommen. Der reguläre Handel an der Tech-Börse Nasdaq beginnt am Freitag.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Google-Suche im KI-Delirium: Halluzination macht aus ehrbarer Firma einen Betrüger. Das darf nicht sein
nzz.description: Die Münchner Richter haben recht. Google soll für den Inhalt seiner KI-Übersicht geradestehen. Innerhalb der Google-Suche gilt: lieber keine KI-Zusammenfassung als eine mit erfundenen Skandalen.

nzz.title: Der «Poulet-Bezwinger» von Saint-Ouen will Präsident von Frankreich werden
nzz.description: Karim Bouamrane führt seit Wochen einen erbitterten Kleinkrieg gegen eine Fast-Food-Kette. Dadurch wurde der Bürgermeister aus der Pariser Banlieue im ganzen Land bekannt. Nun will er bei der Präsidentschaftswahl 2027 antreten.

nzz.title: Prinzessin Bha ist tot. Thailands mystifizierte Monarchie lebt – doch wie lange noch?
nzz.description: Prinzessin Bajrakitiyabha lag seit einem Infarkt vor dreieinhalb Jahren im Koma. Sie war beliebt und galt als wichtige Bezugsperson des thailändischen Königs. Am Donnerstagabend starb sie – und offenbart ein Königshaus in der Krise.

nzz.title: Kolumbiens Präsident postet «Heil Hitler» – und steckt auch sonst in der Klemme
nzz.description: Gustavo Petro hat mit einem Nazi-Vergleich die Israeli erzürnt. Dass es in Kolumbien Versuche gibt, ihn vorzeitig absägen, hat aber andere Gründe. Der Wahlkampf nimmt irre Wendungen.

nzz.title: Letztes Jahr gewann er noch die Vendée Globe, nun ist er mit 42 Jahren gestorben: Frankreich trauert um seinen Segelhelden

nzz.title: Beschwingt, aber nicht originell: Mit Shakira wird im Aztekenstadion von Mexiko die Fussball-WM eröffnet
nzz.description: Beim Programm ging die Fifa kein Risiko ein. Der heimliche Star war das Stadion.

nzz.title: DATENANALYSE - Diesel-Tankrabatt kam nie vollständig an – der tägliche Spritpreis-Check für Deutschland

nzz.description: Der Altnationalrat Hans Kaufmann ist kurz vor seinem 78. Geburtstag gestorben. Abschied von einem Fachpolitiker alter Schule.

nzz.title: «Pour la cohésion de la Suisse»: Der Bundesrat will das Frühfranzösisch im Gesetz verankern
nzz.description: Der Thurgau hat es im April beschlossen, Zürich und St. Gallen im Herbst: Französisch soll es nicht mehr auf Primarstufe geben. Innenministerin Baume-Schneider sieht den Zusammenhalt der Schweiz gefährdet und will das Sprachengesetz anpassen. Nun ist die Vernehmlassung eröffnet worden.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Impressionen der Fussball-WM 2026
nzz.description: Drei Länder, 48 Nationen: Vom 11. Juni bis zum 19. Juli findet die Fussball-Weltmeisterschaft der Männer in Mexiko, Kanada und den USA statt. Einblicke in die WM in Bildern.

nzz.title: Weltklasse vom Land – warum die Schweizer 800-m-Läuferin Audrey Werro um den Weltrekord läuft
nzz.description: Die 22-jährige Leichtathletin hat sich vom scheuen Mädchen zur selbstbewussten Chefin im Feld gewandelt. Doch wie schnell sie nun rennt, überrascht sogar ihre Trainerin.

nzz.title: PODCAST «NZZ WEEKEND» - «Ich finde Architektur nicht so spannend», sagt Jacques Herzog, der die Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg und die Tate Modern in London entworfen hat
nzz.description: Der weltberühmte Basler Architekt gibt sich so persönlich wie noch nie. Er spricht über seine Anfänge, sein Erfolgsgeheimnis, seine lebenslange Freundschaft mit Pierre de Meuron und darüber, warum er immer noch seine Eltern vermisst.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Wasserversorgung in Donezk nach ukrainischem Angriff unterbrochen

spiegel.title: »Tagesspiegel«: Stephan-Andreas Casdorff muss Tätigkeiten ruhen lassen
spiegel.description: Statt selbst zu schreiben, ließ ein Journalist des »Tagesspiegel« seine Meinungsbeiträge von einer KI verfassen. Die Zeitung zieht nun Konsequenzen.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump und Iran: Die wichtigsten Aussagen über den Zustand des Abkommens
spiegel.description: Mal droht Donald Trump mit harten Schlägen, dann soll eine Einigung mit Iran wieder kurz bevorstehen. Und auch die Gegenseite sendet unterschiedliche Signale. Ein Überblick über das Kommunikationschaos zwischen Washington und Teheran.

spiegel.title: Mykorrhiza-Netzwerke: Wie Pilze unterirdisch unsere ganze Welt umspannen
spiegel.description: Mykorrhiza-Pilze setzen sich auf Pflanzenwurzeln und breiten sich so immer weiter aus. Ihre Netzwerke sind so dicht und lang, dass man damit 750 Mal von der Erde zur Sonne käme.

spiegel.title: Fall Jeffrey Epstein: Was wusste seine Assistentin Sarah Kellen?
spiegel.description: Sarah Kellen war Epsteins persönliche Assistentin, die US-Justiz führte sie als »Mittäterin«. Was ihre Aussage vor einem parlamentarischen Ausschuss über das System Epstein verrät.

spiegel.title: WM 2026: Jürgen Klopp, Almuth Schult, Christian Streich – alle TV-Experten im Überblick
spiegel.description: Die WM ist mit 104 Spielen so groß wie nie. Und auch in Sachen Fußballexpertise bieten die TV-Sender ein selten gesehenes Staraufgebot. Hier können Sie Ihren Favoriten wählen – oder Ihre Favoritin.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump: Wunschdenken vom Kriegsende mit Iran vor dem Geburtstag
spiegel.description: »Wir haben heute den Krieg mit Iran beendet«, erklärt der US-Präsident lapidar in einer Telefonkonferenz mit einem weniger bekannten Parteikollegen. Wie Trump sich den Deal herbeiredet – im Video.

spiegel.title: Großbritannien: Keir Starmer kündigt harten Machtkampf um sein Amt an
spiegel.description: Trotz wachsender Kritik will der britische Premierminister Keir Starmer um sein Amt kämpfen. Er macht klar: Wer ihn stürzen will, muss sich auf einen harten Machtkampf einstellen.

spiegel.title: Frankfurt am Main: Ex-Student berichtet über 26.700 Euro Miet-Rückzahlung
spiegel.description: Jahrelang zahlten drei Studenten zu viel Miete im Frankfurter Nordend. Jetzt können sie sich über eine fünfstellige Rückzahlung freuen. Anruf bei einem der früheren Mitbewohner.

spiegel.title: Flughafen München: Bahn sieht keine Möglichkeit für ICE-Anbindung
spiegel.description: Seit der Eröffnung des Münchner Flughafens wünschen sich Fluggäste, Kommunal- und Landespolitiker einen Anschluss an den Fernverkehr der Bahn. Jetzt hat sich selbst die Hoffnung auf eine Behelfslösung zerschlagen.

spiegel.title: Buckelwal in der Ostsee: Till Backhaus redet sich das Wal-Desaster schön
spiegel.description: Daten eines GPS-Trackers sollen belegen, dass der Buckelwal nach der umstrittenen Rettung tagelang weiterlebte. So hat es Minister Till Backhaus verkündet. Doch interne Dokumente zeigen, dass seine eigenen Leute Zweifel haben.

spiegel.title: David Hockney in Bildern: Ein Leben in Farben. Fotostrecke zum Tod des Künstlers
spiegel.description: Er liebte das Licht und die leuchtenden Farben, deswegen zog der gebürtige Nordengländer nach Kalifornien. Später malte er britische Landschaften auf dem iPad. Bilder aus dem Leben von David Hockney, der nun gestorben ist.

spiegel.title: Beleidigungen: Spitzenpolitiker sollen Sonderstatus verlieren
spiegel.description: Die Justizminister wollen die Sonderregelung zum Schutz von Spitzenpolitikern abschaffen. Eine Gruppe soll aber weiter geschützt werden.

phys-org.title: Venus flytrap's snap may come from rapid cell wall softening, not water flow
phys-org.description: The Venus flytrap (Dionaea muscipula) is a marvel of nature, a highly effective killer that doesn't have to move an inch to capture and kill its prey. It releases a fruity nectar scent to attract flies and other insects. After they land in the trap, tiny hairs are triggered and the leaves shut with impressive speed.

phys-org.title: Aliens might exist, but there are three reasons why they're not visiting us
phys-org.description: The United States government's recent release of hundreds of previously classified unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAPs) cases spanning the 1940s to the present, along with the new Steven Spielberg movie, "Disclosure Day," about extraterrestrial life, has fueled the idea that aliens are visiting Earth.

phys-org.title: Why chickens come in so many colors, and what one gene reveals about evolution
phys-org.description: From snow white and jet black to golden brown, domestic chickens display a wider range of plumage colors than almost any other livestock species. A new international study, with researchers from Leipzig University playing a key role, explains why: A single gene is capable of producing this full spectrum. The study provides an example of how genetic diversity and visible traits can emerge within a short evolutionary period. The findings have now been published in the Proceedings of the National A

phys-org.title: DNA tracking links raccoons to riverborne bacteria with possible human spillover
phys-org.description: The emerging infectious bacterium Escherichia albertii has caused outbreaks of severe food poisoning and hospitalized people through contaminated water and foods, such as salad ingredients. Now, a new study from Osaka Metropolitan University (OMU) has gathered evidence from river, animal and genetic samples that suggests a pathway by which invasive raccoons (Procyon lotor) transmit infections to humans.

phys-org.title: What Amazonian photographs reveal when we look again, and together
phys-org.description: A new paper by Junia Mortimer, Urban Studies Foundation fellow, explores what happens when photographic archives are revisited through different conceptual frameworks, and with different people in the room. phys-org.title: Swapping steak for salmon could boost health and reduce emissions
phys-org.description: Swapping a beef steak for salmon once a week could save the amount of carbon needed to fly from London Heathrow to Morocco, according to new research by the universities of Bristol and Southampton. The study, published in Environmental Research: Food Systems, found the U.K.'s current level of meat consumption is 2 to 3 times higher than recommended guidelines.

phys-org.title: Slime molds make decisions using internal fluid flows
phys-org.description: Despite lacking brains or nervous systems, slime molds are capable of making surprisingly sophisticated decisions: navigating mazes, finding food and even remembering where they found it last time. How they manage to do all this without any neural architecture has long puzzled researchers.

phys-org.title: Can ancient bacteria help solve one of agriculture's biggest challenges?
phys-org.description: During the Archean Eon—roughly 4 billion years ago—the Earth was a lifeless planet. The atmosphere lacked oxygen, and there were few, if any, organisms to be found anywhere on the globe. Then something incredible happened. Microscopic bacteria appeared in freshwater lakes, likely in what is now present-day Australia. These bacteria—known now as cyanobacteria—had the near-magical ability to convert sunlight and water into oxygen and other chemical energy.

phys-org.title: Ancient DNA study of post-Roman Europeans reveals emergence of complex new society
phys-org.description: A new study from the HistoGenes project, of which Patrick Geary, professor emeritus in the School of Historical Studies, is co-PI, is helping scholars frame a better picture of the early medieval people who inhabited Western Europe after the fall of the Roman Empire, as well as the societies they created.

phys-org.title: Antarctic surface melt could jump tenfold this century as warming spreads south
phys-org.description: New research shows surface melting across Antarctica is set to intensify and spread dramatically over the 21st century, with melt increasing 10-fold and the affected area growing by more than 10% by 2100 if global temperatures continue to rise.

phys-org.title: Can the cataclysmic explosions of dying stars help unlock grand mysteries of the universe?
phys-org.description: Once charted as a 'guest star' in ancient China, dreaded as a harbinger of ill omens in medieval Europe, and preserved in the narratives and artworks of Indigenous cultures, these cosmic spectacles are now known as core-collapse supernovae.

phys-org.title: 'Puffy' super-Neptune emerges 383 light-years away with a density of just 0.4 g/cm³
phys-org.description: Using the Subaru Telescope, astronomers have conducted follow-up observations of a recently discovered exoplanet known as TOI-1883 b. Results of the new observations, published June 5 on the arXiv preprint server, indicate that TOI-1883 b is a low-density super-Neptune.

phys-org.title: Tracking the Antarctic ice most at risk of breakup and melting
phys-org.description: Antarctic sea ice plays a critical role in regulating Earth's climate. It reflects sunlight back into space, insulates the ocean from the atmosphere, and supports unique polar ecosystems.

phys-org.title: Study offers guidance to schools looking to create outdoor education programs
phys-org.description: Just outside the doors of Stearns Junior-Senior High School in Millinocket, Maine, students and staff have access to world-class outdoor recreation opportunities: paddling, mountain biking, skiing and, of course, hiking in nearby Baxter State Park.

phys-org.title: Growing energy efficiency divide making renters sweat
phys-org.description: Households are motivated to reduce their energy consumption and help mitigate climate change, but unaffordable technologies and rental restrictions are preventing them from doing so, according to a recent Charles Darwin University (CDU) study. "The efficiency divide: Housing constraints on energy-saving practices in Darwin, Australia" was published in the journal Energy Research & Social Science.

phys-org.title: Reeling in labor abuse: Building tools to improve accountability in the fishing industry
phys-org.description: In 2020, the International Seafood Sustainability Foundation approached Stanford's Center for Ocean Solutions (COS) to help identify priorities for action on social sustainability issues in seafood supply chains. After years of collaboration with a range of partners, the result is IKAN, a digital platform designed to support migrant fishers in better understanding their rights, tracking whether contract terms are being met, and accessing information and support if problems arise.

phys-org.title: Engineering quantum Hall stripes in 2D materials inside electromagnetic cavities
phys-org.description: Quantum materials, materials with properties that are governed by the laws of quantum mechanics, have proved to be highly promising for the development of ultra-efficient electronic devices, quantum processors, highly precise sensors and various other technologies. Reliably controlling these materials' quantum phases would be highly advantageous, as it would enable engineers to tailor and optimize their properties for specific applications.

phys-org.title: Brains update sensory predictions through single timing hub, electric fish study finds
phys-org.description: In the split second after you hear a noise, your brain is already making a potentially life-or-death deduction: Did I do that, or did something else? Our nervous systems answer this question using something called corollary discharge, a copy of a motor command that tells sensory areas what to expect from our own actions. This mechanism is at the center of a new study by biologists at Washington University in St. Louis, published in Current Biology.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

public-dom.description: A philosophical system and a practical guide for the cultivation of dramatic genius.

public-dom.title: The Launch of Our Mid-Year Fundraiser!
public-dom.description: Our Mid-Year Fundraiser is launched, and the new postcards theme will be Soil.

public-dom.title: Covers from Cerîde-i Adliye, a Turkish Law Journal (1924–26)
public-dom.description: Legal infographics that reflect a Turkish nation in flux.

public-dom.title: Animal, Vegetable, Lamb: The Zoophyte from Tartary
public-dom.description: In the Middle Ages, rumours spread across Europe of a strange hybrid creature, half-animal, half-plant, known as the Vegetable Lamb of Tartary. A hoax based on fern rhizomes? A euphemism for culled fetal lambs? Or perhaps a medieval misapprehension of cotton? Thom Sliwowski traces the roots of this fabled zoophyte.

public-dom.title: The Prophecies of the Brahan Seer (1877)

proj-syn.title: The Democrats Need a Story, Not More Lists
proj-syn.description: Whereas Donald Trump has offered voters a clear and compelling narrative, Democrats have provided only vague aspirations and long lists of policies. To win over voters—rather than scrounging protest votes—they must articulate a compelling economic vision, with wage-led growth as its foundation.

proj-syn.title: What if Europe Loses Access to Its Climate Data?
proj-syn.description: The European Green Deal runs on data, from corporate disclosures to climate-risk analyses and decarbonization pathways. proj-syn.title: Raising Interest Rates Won’t Stabilize African Inflation
proj-syn.description: Monetary tightening in Africa would not only fail to rein in inflation; it would raise the cost of productive investment, suppress growth, and hamper the continent's much-needed structural transformation. A better strategy would focus on accelerating this transformation by channeling finance into productive industries.

proj-syn.title: The Enduring Enigma of Economic Growth
proj-syn.description: Developing countries have made enormous progress in many of the factors behind growth, reflected in stronger institutions, rising education levels, higher life expectancy, and increased investment rates. proj-syn.title: Brazil’s Bad Vibes
proj-syn.description: A government that abandons structural agendas whenever sentiment turns negative will still be managing sentiment four years later—with nothing to show for it. Brazil’s “vibecession” is a real problem for the current government; but winning the news cycle is not a real solution.

proj-syn.title: Negotiating With the Antichrist
proj-syn.description: Apocalyptic thinking is seeping into the political discourse, with figures like Peter Thiel, Pete Hegseth, and Aleksandr Dugin portraying political differences as struggles between good and evil. When rivals become mortal enemies, the instruments of politics and diplomacy cannot work.

proj-syn.title: Why Is Europe’s Economy Falling Short?
proj-syn.description: For much of the postwar era, European policymakers have prioritized stability and predictability over fostering breakthrough innovation. Today, as the United States and China compete for AI dominance, a stagnant Europe is struggling to regain its place at the technological frontier.

proj-syn.title: Big Tech’s Shadow Market Power
proj-syn.description: Big Tech firms are amassing market power through strategies that bypass current rules for oversight, investigation, and intervention. Unless and until regulators account for the full scope and scale of these strategies, Silicon Valley’s dominance will remain unchallenged.

proj-syn.title: The AI Revolution Mirrors the Green Transition
proj-syn.description: The need for massive upfront investments and the likelihood of significant job displacement imply remarkable parallels between the AI buildout and the green transition. In both cases, the state has an important role to play in guiding market forces on behalf of the public good.

proj-syn.title: Where Is China’s Trillion-Dollar Trade Surplus Going?
proj-syn.description: Whereas China’s trade surplus used to be absorbed largely by the central bank and channeled into official reserves, it is now being redeployed by private actors in search of yield. This indicates China’s progress on financial deepening and underscores markets' increasingly central role in shaping the economy.

proj-syn.title: The Future of Development Finance Is Not Primarily About Money
proj-syn.description: Multilateral development banks have not kept pace with changes to the global financial environment. For middle-income countries like India, accessing knowledge and technology is now a bigger challenge than raising capital, which suggests that these institutions must rethink their operating model.
